  From September 1 to 11, 2027, this itinerary links Quito, Quilotoa Lake, the waterfalls of Baños, two nights at Casa del Suizo on the Napo River, the thermal springs of Papallacta, and the Galápagos Islands. Santa Cruz features giant tortoises, a dedicated trip to Bartolomé, and one of two alternative island excursions.

## Ecuador: the Andes, Amazon and Galápagos, September 1–11, 2027

This **11-day, 10-night** itinerary brings together three natural environments in Ecuador. In the Andes, travelers explore historic Quito, a high-altitude lake and waterfalls. They then descend for several days into the warm Napo River basin before heading to the oceanic islands of the Galápagos archipelago.

What distinguishes the Ada Tours itinerary is that you genuinely change where you stay. A city hotel, an Amazonian lodge, a thermal resort and a hotel on [Santa Cruz Island](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/) each serve a different purpose. When comparing tours, therefore, look at the time spent in each section rather than only the overall figure of 11 days.

## September 1–2: Quito and the equator

The first day is devoted to arrival in Quito, hotel check-in and an evening meeting with the guide. The next introduces the historic districts of the capital and sights along the equator. The city sits high in the Andes and is known for its colonial architecture; its historic center is protected by UNESCO.

Around the city, travelers visit sites connected with Ecuador's geographical history. [Quito and the Cotopaxi area](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/) are well suited to the opening days, when acclimatizing to the altitude matters before further journeys.

## September 3–4: Quilotoa, Tigua and the Baños waterfalls

On the third day, the route enters the Central Andes. Near the village of Tigua, travelers discover local decorative art before heading to [Quilotoa crater lake](/ecuador/place/quilotoa-lake/). From the rim, there are views over the volcanic lake and its unusually colored water.

The next stop is [Baños](/ecuador/place/banos/) and the surrounding valleys. The itinerary includes the Agoyán, Bride's Veil and Pailón del Diablo waterfalls. This region is known for steep, green slopes and water plunging from the heights toward the road.

Activities have different inclusion rules. The main sightseeing stops form part of the itinerary, while kayaking or a return ride by mule at Quilotoa, canopy activities in Baños and other optional experiences cost extra. If you have a particular sport in mind, check in advance how much time is allocated to it.

## September 5–7: the Amazon and Papallacta

On September 5, the road descends from the Andes toward Tena and the [Napo River](/ecuador/place/napo-river/). At Punta Ahuano, guests board a canoe for the trip to Casa del Suizo Lodge. The Amazon section covers **3 days and 2 nights** at this lodge.

On September 6, the nature program takes place with a local guide. Guests choose an appropriate combination of the offered activities, including forest walks and river outings. Several independent excursion modules are listed as alternatives: they should not be understood as a compulsory sequence of every activity on the same day.

On September 7, guests return to the highlands and [Papallacta](/ecuador/place/papallacta/). Time is set aside to relax in the thermal springs after the hot Amazon section. The natural contrast is particularly evident in the weather and clothing: evenings high in the mountains are much cooler than on the river.

## September 8–11: the Galápagos and marine excursions

A flight to the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) is scheduled for September 8. After landing on [Baltra](/ecuador/place/baltra-island/), the route crosses the Itabaca Channel to [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/). In the island's highlands, giant tortoises can be seen in their natural habitat; a visit to lava tunnels is also included.

September 9 features a dedicated boat trip to [Bartolomé Island](/ecuador/place/bartolome-island/), prized for its volcanic terrain, island panoramas and marine excursion. The return to Puerto Ayora is scheduled for the afternoon.

On September 10, **one of two alternative island itineraries** is planned:

| Option | Visits |
|---|---|
| [North Seymour](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) | Together with Bachas Beach |
| [South Plaza](/ecuador/place/south-plaza-island/) | Together with Cape Carrión |

The specific island is confirmed after booking. These are not two consecutive excursion days but a choice between two planned routes. Lunch on board and a free evening are also scheduled for this day.

On September 11, a transfer takes guests to Baltra Airport for a flight back to the mainland, to Quito or [Guayaquil](/ecuador/place/guayaquil/). From there, travelers continue on an international flight.

## Tour price and room occupancy

| Accommodation | Price per person |
|---|---:|
| Triple occupancy | $4 157 |
| Double occupancy | $4 260 |
| Single occupancy | $4 917 |

These are the rates for the **September 1–11, 2027** itinerary, not universal prices for any trip through Ecuador. They apply to the listed hotels or equivalent accommodation: Finlandia in Quito, La Floresta in Baños, Casa del Suizo Lodge in the Amazon, Termas de Papallacta and Fiesta on Santa Cruz.

The price includes **10 nights**, group transfers and scheduled excursions, meals as specified for each day, the stated entrance tickets and the Galápagos Transit Control Card. A Russian-speaking guide accompanies the mainland portion and an English-speaking guide the islands; the first and last transfers have separate language arrangements.

International flights, the Quito–Galápagos–Quito or Guayaquil flight, medical insurance, personal expenses and the Galápagos National Park entry fee are paid separately. The indicated park fee is approximately $200, with a discount for children under 12; the applicable fee depends on park administration rules on the date of the visit.

## Practical details worth knowing in advance

The group is limited to a maximum of 15 people. With so many climate zones, you will need clothing for the cool Andes, humid Amazon and boat trips. Some outings require early departures, while accommodation changes and flights make transfer days quite busy.

The Galápagos are a protected area with visitor and biosecurity rules. Animals must not be fed; visitors should keep their distance and remain on permitted routes. Arranging transfers through Baltra, ticket logistics and sufficient check-in time require particular attention.

Allow **at least 4 hours** between the return flight from the Galápagos to the mainland and an international departure. An early international flight may require an additional night in Quito or Guayaquil; that night is not included in the basic 11-day itinerary.

## How this itinerary differs from other Ecuador tours

If you would rather spend more time in high-altitude reserves, cloud forests and an Amazonian lodge, consider the [15-day mainland Ecuador tour](/ecuador/tour/mainland-ecuador-amazon-15-days/). It does not include the Galápagos, but offers a much longer exploration of the northern Andes and Amazonian nature.

If your aim is to watch humpback whales during the viewing season and relax by the Pacific, there is a separate [August itinerary, “Ecuador, the Galápagos and Humpback Whales”](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-humpback-whales/). It is not simply a version of the September trip: the dates, regional sequence and included services differ.

## Frequently asked questions about the September 1–11, 2027 tour

### How long do travelers spend in the Amazon?

Three days and two nights at Casa del Suizo Lodge. Nature activities are selected with the local guide, so not all of the listed options take place in one day.

### Are domestic flights to the Galápagos included?

No. The flight to the islands and the return to Quito or Guayaquil are charged separately.

### Will we definitely visit both North Seymour and South Plaza?

No. September 10 includes one of two island itineraries. The specific option is confirmed at booking.

### Which Galápagos park entry expenses are included?

The Transit Control Card is included in the tour price, while the National Park entrance fee is paid separately. They are two distinct payments.

### Can we fly home immediately after returning from the islands?

The itinerary allows for an onward international flight, but recommends at least a 4-hour connection. An early flight may require an extra night's stay.

## Ecuador and the Galápagos in 14 days: what makes this nature itinerary different

This journey alternates between **the Andes, cloud forest and oceanic islands**. The opening days take you through [Quito and the Cotopaxi area](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/), [Quilotoa crater lake](/ecuador/place/quilotoa-lake/) and [Baños](/ecuador/place/banos/). Three days then follow in the [Mashpi Reserve](/ecuador/place/mashpi-reserve/), with the final section devoted to the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/).

The itinerary lasts **14 days and 13 nights**. Choose it for the variety of natural regions rather than the maximum number of sights packed into a day. As the route moves from a high-altitude park to humid forest and the coast, temperatures, clothing, footwear and excursion formats change. Travelers seeking more demanding mountain activities may prefer the separate [17-day adventure itinerary](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-adventure-17-days/).

## The Andes: Cotopaxi, Quilotoa and Baños

The journey begins in Quito, with time for the historic center and the equator area. It then heads into the Cotopaxi region, with its high-altitude landscapes and Limpiopungo Lake. Another major stop is Quilotoa, a crater lake surrounded by mountains; the road then continues to the waterfalls and canyon of Baños.

Much of the mainland section takes place at considerable altitude. Even without technical mountaineering, you may feel different from how you do at home: gradual acclimatization, sun protection, warm clothing and a sensible walking pace are important. Travelers with heart or lung conditions should discuss the effects of altitude with a doctor before departure.

In [Baños](/ecuador/place/banos/), the itinerary centers on the waterfalls and landscapes of the Pastaza Valley. This offers a different natural experience from the highlands, with more lush vegetation, rivers and sheer slopes.

## Mashpi: why the forest gets three days

[Mashpi](/ecuador/place/mashpi-reserve/) is more than a brief sightseeing stop. The itinerary includes several days staying at a lodge, walking in the cloud forest and taking part in nature activities at different times of day. Weather, the group's preparedness and trail conditions determine the precise order of outings; forest activities cannot be reduced to one fixed timetable.

This section features **group excursions with an English-speaking guide**, while transfers between Quito and Mashpi Lodge are shared, with a driver. A private guide in Mashpi and SPA services are not included in the basic package. For guests who value a private experience, this is an important difference from the mainland excursions, which include a Russian-speaking guide-interpreter.

Mashpi is particularly rewarding for those willing to observe the forest without expecting a particular animal on every outing. In the humid forest, birds and other inhabitants are often heard before they appear among the vegetation. A light rain jacket, moisture-protected equipment and closed shoes help make observation more comfortable.

## Santa Cruz, Bartolomé and Isabela: different sides of the Galápagos

The island section begins on day nine. On [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/), the itinerary introduces giant tortoises and volcanic landscapes, followed by a boat excursion to [Bartolomé](/ecuador/place/bartolome-island/). On one of the following days, there is **a choice: North Seymour or South Plaza**. This means selecting one option, not a promise to visit both islands in a single day.

The route then continues to [Isabela](/ecuador/place/isabela-island/), where visits include Tintoreras, [Sierra Negra Volcano](/ecuador/place/sierra-negra-volcano/) and Concha de Perla Bay. The volcanic landscapes on land and the sea excursions have different requirements: some sections call for comfortable hiking shoes and sun protection, while others require attention to sea conditions, possible swell and safe boarding of boats.

Galápagos wildlife is famous for endemic species, but the chance of encountering any particular animal depends on the island, season and actual itinerary. A list of the archipelago's entire fauna should not be mistaken for guaranteed sightings on any specific day.

## Services and expenses to compare

On the mainland, private transfers and excursions with a Russian-speaking guide-interpreter are provided. In Mashpi and the Galápagos, the activities are shared programs with English-speaking guides. Accommodation, scheduled meals and specified entrance tickets are included. The tour price is **$8236**.

International airfare, the **Quito–Galápagos–Guayaquil or Quito** flight, the archipelago's national park entrance fee, the immigration card, insurance, tips and personal expenses are listed separately. Official fees may change; before booking, check the Galápagos National Park rules applicable to the traveler's citizenship and category.

The mix of private and group sections matters when choosing a trip. If your main interest is watching animals in Ecuador's natural areas, see also the [selection of wildlife tours in Ecuador](/interests/wildlife/tours/ecuador/).

## Frequently asked questions about the Ecuador nature tour

### Does this trip include climbing Cotopaxi?

The itinerary visits Cotopaxi's high-altitude areas and natural sights, but a technical ascent to the summit is not part of the main program. This is a nature tour, not a sporting mountaineering expedition.

### Are excursions to all the named islands included?

The itinerary includes specific stops on Santa Cruz, Bartolomé and Isabela, but one sea-excursion day offers a choice of North Seymour **or** South Plaza. The exact option depends on the agreed program.

### Are all excursions led by a Russian-speaking guide?

No. The mainland section uses a Russian-speaking guide-interpreter, while Mashpi and the Galápagos offer group excursions in English.

### Is the flight to the Galápagos included in the tour price?

No. Flights between the mainland and archipelago are paid for separately, along with government fees and the immigration card.

## Ecuador and the Galápagos in 8 days: Quito, Mindo, Quilotoa and Isabela

Eight days are enough to discover several of Ecuador's natural regions: high-altitude [Quito and its surroundings](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/), [Mindo](/ecuador/place/mindo/) cloud forest, [Quilotoa](/ecuador/place/quilotoa-lake/) crater lake and the volcanic [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). The itinerary covers **8 days and 7 nights**: the first four days are on the mainland, and the next four include a flight to the archipelago, island visits and the return journey.

**No specific departure dates have been set** for this tour. The departure month and availability of a suitable trip must be confirmed separately.

## The mainland section: four different excursion days

| Day | Main itinerary |
|---|---|
| 1 | Arrival and introduction to Quito |
| 2 | Historic Quito and equator-related sites |
| 3 | Mindo cloud forest |
| 4 | Mountain route to Quilotoa via Tigua |

The capital sits high in the Andes. The sightseeing program includes squares, churches, viewpoints and places associated with the equator. The altitude changes matter during the first days: after a flight and time in the city, the route proceeds into even higher mountain areas.

[Mindo](/ecuador/place/mindo/) reveals a very different Ecuador. The humid forest is known for its wealth of birds and plants; possible sightings include hummingbirds and orchids. Optional activities such as ziplining require attention to operator rules and physical readiness. Observing wild birds can be fascinating, but no particular species or number of sightings can be guaranteed.

On the way to [Quilotoa](/ecuador/place/quilotoa-lake/), there is a stop at Tigua, where local artistic traditions continue. At the crater, the group may choose to stay at the viewpoint; a more active option involves descending toward the water. Climbing back is especially demanding because of the altitude and the walker's fitness, so it is best to agree on the walking plan before the excursion begins.

## The Galápagos: Santa Cruz Island and a sea excursion to Isabela

On day five, travelers fly from the mainland to the archipelago. On [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/), they encounter giant land tortoises and volcanic landscapes, including lava tunnels. The sixth day is dedicated to a sea excursion to [Isabela](/ecuador/place/isabela-island/) and natural areas inhabited by sea lions, iguanas, birds and other island wildlife.

The Galápagos are a UNESCO World Heritage protected area with special conservation rules. Animals must not be fed or disturbed, and landings and walks follow approved routes. Day seven is free, allowing time to rest after the boat trip, although optional activities and their costs should not automatically be treated as included.

Day eight is devoted to departure from the islands. An onward international connection requires separate consideration of the domestic flight schedule and airline rules.

## Guides and transfers in different regions

On the mainland, the program includes group transfers and excursions with **a Russian-speaking guide or driver-guide**. On the Galápagos, excursions are accompanied by **an English-speaking guide**. The final transfer from the island hotel to the airport is with a Spanish-speaking escort, without a separate excursion guide.

This is an important condition for anyone expecting Russian-speaking assistance throughout all eight days. The language depends on the region and specific stage, so agree on a format that works for your group in advance.

## Calculating the cost: flights and fees are separate

The base tour price is **$1 960**, while island flights and mandatory charges are listed as separately payable services. Under this tour's conditions:

- Quito–Galápagos–Quito or Guayaquil flight: **$575 per person**.
- Galápagos National Park entrance fee: **$200 per person**; the description specifies a discount for children under 12.
- TCT/INGALA Transit Control Card: **$20 per person**.
- International airfare, insurance, tips and personal expenses are also paid separately.

The official Galápagos National Park rules set categories of admission fees by age and nationality. The published charge for a regular international visitor over 12 is **$200**, but other rates apply to certain nationalities and categories. The TCT is arranged separately. Check the current applicable rate with the official service before confirming the trip.

The included services consist of accommodation and meals according to the itinerary, group excursions and transfers, regional guide services and entrance tickets to the listed sites, excluding the island park fee explicitly charged separately.

## When to choose this particular route

This trip suits travelers who want to experience both Andean Ecuador and island wildlife during a short vacation. The mainland itinerary is fairly intensive, while the archipelago offers one free day after the sea excursion. Those who prefer a comfortable lodge stay in the cloud forest and additional boat outings on the islands can compare it with the [nine-day Mashpi and Galápagos itinerary](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-quito-cotopaxi-mashpi-galapagos-9-days/).

Find more options in the [Ecuador tour catalogue](/ecuador/tour/) and the [Nature](/interests/nature/) and [Wildlife and Safari](/interests/wildlife/) sections.

## Frequently asked questions about the Quito–Quilotoa–Galápagos tour

### How many days are devoted to the Galápagos?

Four calendar days, including the flight there on day five and the departure on day eight. One day is free.

### Where does the Russian-speaking guide work?

On the mainland portion. Galápagos excursions are conducted with English-speaking guides.

### Is airfare from the mainland to the islands included?

No. It is listed as an additional expense, with the amount specified separately in the itinerary conditions.

### Is a separate transit card required?

Yes. The TCT is used to enter the Galápagos, while visiting the protected areas requires a separate entrance fee.

### Are the exact travel dates stated?

No. The current tour listing does not specify a departure date. The calendar is arranged separately.

## Ecuador and the Galápagos with an 18-day cruise itinerary: what makes it different

**This is a nature journey through three very different environments:** an Amazonian river and tropical rainforest, the Andes and their cloud forests, and finally oceanic islands. During the **18 days and 17 nights**, the opening days focus on [Coca](/ecuador/place/coca/), the [Napo River](/ecuador/place/napo-river/) and the [Sacha Reserve](/ecuador/place/sacha-reserve/); the middle section explores Ecuador's volcanoes, highlands and forests, and the finale is a four-day cruise aboard **M/Y Grand Majestic**.

Compared with the [14-day Mashpi and island-excursion tour](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-nature-discovery/), this itinerary has a separate Amazon section and ends with a seagoing cruise. If you prefer to return to a hotel on the same island every night, a land-based trip may be more convenient. If you want to visit several different islands on a single cruise, the yacht offers a different way to organize the journey.

## The Amazon: staying at Sacha Lodge and exploring the river

After arrival in Quito, the program includes a flight to Coca, followed by a river journey to Sacha Lodge. The Amazon itinerary features forest trails, bird and monkey watching, canopy walks and canoe exploration of flooded forest. Named natural sites include Pilchicocha Lake and the Lagartococha area.

Staying in the lodge allows guests to experience the forest at different times of day. At dawn, dusk and after rainfall, sounds and animal behavior change, although no encounter with a particular species can be guaranteed. Rain and insect protection, closed shoes and waterproof packaging for documents and cameras will make the trip more comfortable.

The Amazon section uses **an English-speaking guide** and group excursions. The **Quito–Coca–Quito** flight is paid for separately. This matters when comparing the total cost with tours that do not include the Amazon.

## Central Ecuador: Otavalo, Pululahua, Bellavista and Quilotoa

The journey then returns to the Andes. Major stops include [Otavalo](/ecuador/place/otavalo/), high-altitude natural areas, Pululahua crater, [Bellavista Cloud Forest](/ecuador/place/bellavista-cloud-forest/) and [Mindo](/ecuador/place/mindo/). Days thirteen and fourteen are spent around Cotopaxi and [Quilotoa Lake](/ecuador/place/quilotoa-lake/).

The contrast in conditions is especially noticeable here: the highlands may call for a warm jacket and wind protection, while the cloud forest requires clothing suited to moisture and insects. The tour is designed around nature observation; it does not feature a five-day high-altitude sporting trek like the [17-day active tour](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-adventure-17-days/).

Excursions in Bellavista are shared; the other mainland sections include private services with a Russian-speaking guide-interpreter or driver-guide. The style of accompaniment is therefore mixed, and the degree of privacy changes from one region to another.

## Four days aboard M/Y Grand Majestic: why this is a cruise

Days fifteen through eighteen feature a cruise aboard **M/Y Grand Majestic**, a 5-star-category yacht. After flying to [San Cristóbal](/ecuador/place/san-cristobal-island/), the route continues to [Floreana](/ecuador/place/floreana-island/) and then [Española](/ecuador/place/espanola-island/), ending via [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/).

This is a continuous voyage aboard a vessel, not a series of separate daily excursions returning to a hotel on land. On Floreana, the named stops are Post Office Bay, Punta Cormorant and Devil's Crown; on Española, they are Punta Suárez and Gardner Bay. Experiences here depend on landing conditions, the sea, permitted routes and wildlife behavior.

Along the way, guests may see sea lions, frigatebirds, boobies and other island wildlife; **the appearance of any particular species on a given day is not guaranteed**. Boat excursions require consideration of possible seasickness, tender operations, the need to follow guides' instructions and Galápagos National Park regulations.

The yacht section makes this itinerary particularly suitable for enthusiasts of [cruises and expeditions](/interests/cruises-and-expeditions/tours/ecuador/), rather than only those interested in Ecuador in general.

## What's included and what you pay separately

The tour includes hotel and yacht accommodation, scheduled transfers and excursions, meals in the specified amount, and admission tickets to the visited sites. Services in the Galápagos, Amazon and Bellavista are shared; elsewhere on the mainland they are private. Guides speak English in the Amazon and islands; on other sections a Russian-speaking guide-interpreter or driver-guide is provided.

The listed tour price is **$10314**. **International tickets and both domestic flight segments** (to Coca and to the Galápagos) are charged separately. National Park government fees and immigration documents, insurance, tips and personal expenses are also extra. Official fees and access rules for protected areas depend on current regulations and visitor category, so they must be checked for the specific journey.

This trip is especially appropriate for people who want to combine several forms of nature observation in one itinerary: a riverside lodge, mountain and cloud forests, then a yacht in the Pacific. Compare more options in the [Ecuador tour catalogue](/ecuador/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about the Galápagos cruise

### Is the entire trip spent aboard a yacht?

No. The cruise occupies the final four days. Before it, the itinerary includes an Amazon lodge and mainland nature excursions.

### Which islands does the cruise cover?

The route passes through San Cristóbal, Floreana, Española and Santa Cruz. Specific landings and activities depend on the program and the rules for visiting protected sites.

### Is every day accompanied by a private guide?

No. Services in the Amazon, Bellavista and the Galápagos are shared, while private excursions and transfers are provided in the other parts of the itinerary.

### Do domestic flight tickets need to be purchased separately?

Yes. Flights on the Quito–Coca–Quito route and between mainland Ecuador and the Galápagos are paid for separately from the main tour price.

## Ecuador in 9 days: Quito, Cotopaxi, Mashpi and the Galápagos Islands

This nine-day program brings together four natural and cultural chapters: historic Quito, the volcanic landscapes of Cotopaxi, the cloud forest of [Mashpi Reserve](/ecuador/place/mashpi-reserve/) and the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). Duration is **9 days and 8 nights**. Unlike a conventional sightseeing route, staying at the nature lodge is itself an important part of the experience.

This journey suits travelers who are happy to change environments several times and value comfortable accommodation alongside nature excursions. The tour listing contains no confirmed travel dates, so flight schedules and hotel availability must be checked for your chosen period.

## The first three days: Quito and Cotopaxi National Park

In Quito, the itinerary includes historic squares, churches and places associated with the equator. The city sits high in the Andes, so the effects of altitude can be felt even on ordinary walks. On day three, the route reaches Cotopaxi National Park.

Stops are planned near the volcano in open high-altitude landscapes and around Limpiopungo Lake. These are scenic and nature excursions; the program does **not promise an ascent of Cotopaxi's summit**. Mountain weather can change rapidly, and temperatures differ considerably from those at sea level.

This section features private transfers and excursions with **a Russian-speaking guide-interpreter**. Before traveling, consider the altitude, wind and your own tolerance for high-altitude walks.

## Mashpi: humid forest instead of highlands

On day four, the road leads from Quito to [Mashpi](/ecuador/place/mashpi-reserve/), and day five continues with nature activities and the return to the capital. This cloud-forest section introduces travelers to plants, birds and other inhabitants of the humid tropical environment.

The program includes a stay at **Mashpi Lodge** in a Wayra Room. Excursions within the natural area take place **in a group with an English-speaking guide**. Transfers between Quito and the lodge are shared and operated by a driver. A private guide at Mashpi and SPA services are charged separately.

That detail distinguishes Mashpi from a private Quito excursion: the service format is different and a personal Russian-speaking naturalist is not included in the package.

## Four calendar days in the Galápagos

On day six, participants fly to the islands and explore [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/), which has natural habitats for giant tortoises and lava tunnels. Day seven is devoted to a marine excursion to [Bartolomé](/ecuador/place/bartolome-island/).

Day eight offers **one of two options**: [North Seymour](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) **or** South Plaza. These are alternative routes, so both islands cannot be presented as guaranteed visits on the same day.

Bartolomé is known for its volcanic scenery and marine activities. On North Seymour, visitors may observe birds and sea lions, while South Plaza offers other island wildlife and coastal landscapes. The actual choice depends on the confirmed vessel itinerary, National Park permits and sea conditions.

Day nine is dedicated to departure from the Galápagos. Island excursions are shared, with **an English-speaking guide**; the final airport transfer is with a driver only.

## Inclusions and additional expenses

The base tour price is **$4 986**. It includes the scheduled accommodation, meals in the stated amount, relevant transfers and excursions, regional guides and entrance tickets to the sites included in the itinerary, except for fees explicitly listed as additional.

International flights, insurance, a private guide and SPA services at Mashpi, and the flight between the mainland and the Galápagos — **$515 per person** — are charged separately. So are the TCT/INGALA Transit Control Card — **$20** — tips and personal expenses.

**An important difference in the rates:** the terms of this nine-day tour quote a Galápagos National Park fee of **$100**, whereas the official schedule applicable to ordinary foreign tourists over 12 shows **$200**, with special reduced categories based on age and nationality. Before payment, the current official visitor category must be applied rather than automatically accepting the older amount in the package description.

Movement of people and biodiversity is controlled on the islands: there are TCT rules, baggage inspections and permitted visitor routes. These measures protect the archipelago's nature, recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

## Frequently asked questions about Mashpi and the Galápagos

### How many nights does the trip last?

Eight nights over nine calendar days, including the mainland and island sections.

### Can we visit North Seymour and South Plaza on the same day?

The program offers a choice: North Seymour **or** South Plaza. Both options cannot be considered confirmed at once.

### Will there be a Russian-speaking guide in Mashpi?

No. Mashpi offers group excursions with an English-speaking guide. A Russian-speaking guide is provided for Quito and Cotopaxi.

### What payments apply to the Galápagos?

Domestic flights, the TCT Transit Control Card and the National Park fee are listed separately. The applicable park rate is checked against current official rules.
